First, we substitute $u={x}^{3}-4.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=3{x}^{2}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{3}-4$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $-\infty $ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-\infty $ | $-12$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{-2}\frac{9{x}^{2}}{({x}^{3}-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{-12}\frac{3}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-12}\frac{3}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u & =3{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-12}{u}^{-2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-{u}^{-1}]}_{a}^{-12} \\  & =-3\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{u}]}_{a}^{-12} \\  & =-3\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-12)}-\frac{1}{a}] \\  & =-3\cdot (-\frac{1}{12}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
